definitions.gloss: spoken language — the form of language used in speech, as opposed to writing; colloquial style
definitions.explanation: Language as it is actually spoken in conversation, including casual phrasing, sentence-ending particles, contractions, and rhythms of speech that differ from the more formal and tightly structured forms used in writing. Contrasts with {書|か}き{言葉|ことば} ('written language').

examples.japanese: これは{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}です。
{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}と{書|か}き{言葉|ことば}は{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Spoken language and written language are different.

examples.japanese: レポートに{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}を{使|つか}ってはいけません。
examples.english: You must not use colloquial language in a report.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{人|ひと}の{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}には{新|あたら}しい{表現|ひょうげん}がたくさん{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: A lot of new expressions appear in the colloquial speech of young people.

notes:
Compound of {話|はな}す ('to speak') and {言葉|ことば} ('words, language'). Literally 'speaking words.'

USAGE:
- Refers to the style of language actually used when speaking, including casual particles (ね, よ, さ), contractions (〜ちゃう, 〜なきゃ), and looser grammar.
- Often contrasted explicitly with {書|か}き{言葉|ことば} in discussions of style, writing advice, and language teaching.
- In writing classes and style guides, using {話|はな}し{言葉|ことば} in formal documents is typically marked as inappropriate.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}と{書|か}き{言葉|ことば}: spoken and written language
- {話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}を{使|つか}う: to use colloquial/spoken language
- {話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}{調|ちょう}: a conversational style/tone
- くだけた{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}: informal spoken language

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口語|こうご}: spoken/colloquial language — a more technical linguistic term; also refers to modern Japanese as opposed to classical {文語|ぶんご}.
- {書|か}き{言葉|ことば}: written language — the direct antonym.
- {会話|かいわ}: conversation — refers to the act of speaking with someone, not the style of language itself.
